meta: The last part of "Your own AI assistant". Chat apps like ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini can connect to Google Calendar, Gmail and Google Drive. Three levels of access, and how far to open the door.
prompt: When am I free this week?

muc.title: How far should you open the door?
muc.text: The last part of the series: chat apps can now connect to your calendar, email and files. The question is how far to open the door and still stay safe.

muc.title: What is a connection?
muc.text: Connecting means you let AI open a door into your account. The permission screen spells out what it's allowed to do.

muc.title: Let it read
muc.text: Level one: let it read. AI looks at your calendar and reads your email to answer your questions. This is the safe level to start with.

muc.title: Let it draft
muc.text: Level two: let it draft. AI writes emails or appointments for you, but you read them and click send yourself.

muc.title: Don't let it act alone yet
muc.text: Level three, sending, deleting or paying on your behalf: not yet. One misunderstanding, and the email is gone or the data is lost.

muc.title: Ask about your calendar, review permissions
muc.text: Connect your calendar and ask when you're free this week. Then go to your Google account's security settings, see which apps have access, and remove the ones you don't use.

muc.title: Your own assistant
muc.text: Now you have your own assistant: it knows who you are, has prompts ready, gives each task a room, reads your documents, works weekly on its own, and only goes where it's allowed. The next series looks at what all this means for your job.
